absorption: Upstream's image build guarantees equivalent runtime-readable/executable source permissions without the fork commands.
contract: The production container normalizes ownership/permissions of copied source so the runtime user can reliably read and execute application files regardless of host checkout metadata.

fork: build the image from a checkout with restrictive-but-valid source metadata and inspect application source ownership/modes as the runtime user.
proof.fork_expected: application source is readable/executable by the configured runtime user after image build.
upstream: inspect post-copy permission handling in the recorded upstream Dockerfile.
proof.upstream_expected: no equivalent source permission normalization is present.

upstream_gap: The recorded upstream base copies source without the fork's explicit post-copy permission normalization.
